newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate stable on inflation data.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate stable on inflation data.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates were down five basis points at 18.20 percent in early trade on Friday in the wake of mild inflation data and downward yields on the U.S. long bond, traders said.
"Inflation figures were very good, and the secondary market always welcomes data at that level," a trader said.

In late trade on Thursday, Banco de Mexico announced the consumer price index had risen by 1.08 percent in April, compared to an average forecast increase of 1.11 percent in a previously conducted Reuters survey.

Dealers said secondary rates had also remained stable, with a slight downward trend, due to lower U.S. long bond yields following comments by U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan interpreted as heralding moderate Fed tightening only.
"A 25-basis-point hike (in U.S. base rates) is not ruled out, which is what the market is expecting," another dealer said, adding, however, that this move had already been dsicounted.
U.S. 30-year Treasury bonds were up 2/32 to yield 6.93 percent.
Overnight rates on bank paper was meanwhile unchnaged at 19.75 percent.
Liquidity of 176 million pesos was slated to return to the system from prior central bank participation.
